gaps.where: Safety alert page (/safety/<checkInId>, opened from the teammate push/email): the alert card (who, place, Planned end, Checked in, Where their phone was, Their phone) and the I reached them button
gaps.gap: Part of this is wrong. The alert is not "only a push and an email". Every push a person's phone is handed is kept under the bell. The worker keeps it after sending (send.ts:277 → private.keep_push_notification), and the teammate's safety_alert push carries path /app/w/<ws>/safety/<checkInId> (ladder.ts:422). read_notification_list (screen-reads.ts:62) returns that path (queries/notification.ts:64-70), so the Assistant can find the checkInId there and call read_safety_alert / do_safety_resolve. Safety pushes are always on (push.ts:55, 225). What is real: (1) A teammate contact with no phone in the app gets only the email (pushAudience needs a registered push device, queue.ts:108), so they have no bell row and no id. (2) The /safety/<checkInId> page is not a page record (schemas/assistant.ts:319-330; RECORD_ROUTES in words.ts:413-420 has no safety). So asking from the alert page carries no id. (3) Nothing tells the model that a Safety notification's path holds the checkInId, so it has to work that out from a raw path.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the alert page is a place the Assistant knows (A safety alert, /safety/[checkInId]), so asking from it names the check-in, even for a teammate who got only the email. read_safety_alert’s words say a Safety notification’s path under the bell ends in the checkInId, and that do_safety_resolve stops the alerts once they reached the person. No new list of alerts was needed.

gaps.where: Members → ⋯ beside a teammate → Edit hours (opens Settings → My calendar for them: Weekly hours, Add time off)
gaps.gap: Members → ⋯ → Edit hours opens My calendar for the teammate (?user=), which saves schedule.set and time_off.add with ownerId (my-calendar.tsx:141-148) for anyone with calendars.manage. update_my_hours never passes ownerId (tools-settings-me.ts:197, 204-214), and no other Assistant tool or SCREEN_ACTION runs schedule.set or time_off.add for someone else. The Assistant knows the way to the screen (settings-map.ts:1001, 'Set someone else’s hours … Members, ⋯ beside them, then Edit hours') but can't do it. Severity is lowered from high: the card says 'Your week' / 'Put time off in your calendar' (tools-settings-me.ts:136-138, 168), so the person would see it was their own calendar before confirming, and the screen way is already given.
gaps.fix: Fixed: update_my_hours takes userId for a teammate, as Members → ⋯ → Edit hours does, for owners and admins, and the card names whose week it is.

gaps.where: Members: Role picker (members.change_role), ⋯ → Remove from workspace (members.remove), ⋯ → Leave workspace on your own row (anyone), Pending invitations → Revoke (invitations.revoke)
gaps.gap: manage_team is offered only with members.invite (tools.ts:577). A Member, who lacks it by default (permissions.ts:116-126), has no way to leave through the Assistant, though membership.remove needs only workspace.read and lets anyone leave (membership.remove.ts:17, 36-50). Someone given members.change_role, members.remove or invitations.revoke but not members.invite is also left out. When an owner or admin passes their own userId, the card reads 'Take <you> off <business>' / 'They lose their way in' (tools-settings-business.ts:362-372) instead of the screen's 'Leave this workspace?' / 'You lose access immediately. An Owner can invite you back later.' (members-table.tsx:283-288). Severity is lowered: by default all four permissions come together for owners and admins, and leaving is rare.
gaps.fix: Fixed: manage_team is offered to everyone. Each change is refused before a card without the permission its button needs (invite and resend: Invite people; role: Change people’s roles; remove: Remove people; cancel: Cancel invitations). Anyone may leave, on a card titled Leave <business>? that says they lose access immediately and an Owner can invite them back.

gaps.where: Members → Pending invitations: each row’s Email, Role, Invited by, Sent · expires, with Resend and Revoke
gaps.gap: For resend_invitation and cancel_invitation the card shows only {Business: workspace.name} (tools-settings-business.ts:373-381). It doesn't show whose invitation it is (email, role) or when it was sent or expires, and the resend card leaves out the screen toast's 'The old link no longer works.' (pending-invitations.tsx:36). The screenRef line is wrong: the file has 130 lines, with the columns at 72-94 and the toasts at 36/43. Severity is lowered: both actions can be undone (re-invite, resend), and the model picks the invitationId from get_settings team, which lists the email.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the resend and cancel cards show the invitation as Pending invitations lists it: Email, Role, Invited by, Sent and Expires (or Sending now), and resend says the old link stops working. One no longer pending is refused before a card.

gaps.where: Phone: More → Settings → My safety, with Add someone (A teammate / Someone outside: Name, Phone, Email, Save) and tapping a contact → Remove
gaps.gap: It's true that the Assistant can't add or remove safety contacts. safety_contact.save and safety_contact.remove (risk 1, workspace.read, commands/safety.ts:371-377,453-458) have no tool, and 'phone.my_safety' is in SETTINGS_NEVER (coverage.ts:889). But the refusal is deliberate, and it's not a dead end: the Assistant can read the contacts (read_safety_mine, screen-reads.ts:77) and gives the exact way there ('in the phone app, open More, then Settings, then My safety', settings-map.ts:1021). The reason given ('only they choose') is weak, since the Assistant acts as the person behind a Confirm. But no recorded owner decision backs it, and the settled rules don't cover it either. Reversing it changes a NEVER entry, so the owner should say yes first. Severity is lowered for that reason.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the owner settled that a person’s own safety contacts are theirs to change on a card. manage_my_safety_contacts adds a teammate or someone outside, or removes one, on a card that says how each is told (an email alone is never asked, so never told). phone.my_safety is in SETTING_TOOLS, out of SETTINGS_NEVER, and update_safety_settings says never anyone else’s contacts.

gaps.where: Phone: an appointment → Check in (Where, Check out by, Share where I am, Check in); the check-in banner → Help (alerts contacts at once)
gaps.gap: safety.check_in (risk 1), safety.help (risk 2) and safety.where are not in SCREEN_ACTIONS (coverage.ts:150-152 has only check_out, extend and resolve), not in NEVER_FOR_THE_ASSISTANT, and run by no Assistant tool. The coverage test only collects /\/v1\/commands\/…/ strings from apps/web and apps/mobile (assistant-coverage.test.ts:47-54). The phone runs these through change('…') and the typed command map (apps/mobile/src/changes/commands.ts:848-857), so all of them (and safety_contact.save/remove) slip past it. 'Check me in at 12 Oak St till 3' or 'I need help' gets nothing, and no reason is given.
gaps.fix: Fixed: my_check_in starts a check-in, adds time and checks out, on its own and only ever the person’s own. ask_for_help runs safety.help on a card that first says to call 911 and names who is told. Sharing where the phone is (safety.where) stays the phone’s, since only the phone knows where it is, and my_check_in says so.

gaps.where: Support access to private records: the page the support email links to (/settings/support-access), and Real Estate’s settings → Support access tab; buttons Allow for 24 hours, Decline, End now, Give support access for 24 hours
gaps.gap: The Assistant can act (do_support_access_grant/decline/end, coverage.ts:153-157) and read (read_support_access_list, screen-reads.ts:80). But nothing in settings-map, places-map or the prompt names where this lives. The page /settings/support-access is not in the settings catalog or the Settings menu. It is reached only from the email link (handlers/support-access.ts:51) and Real Estate deal settings → Support access tab (deal-settings.tsx:95). Severity is lowered: the prompt says to say it isn't sure rather than guess (prompt.ts:38), so the person gets 'not sure', not a made-up path.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the places map has Support access (/settings/support-access), reached from support’s email or Real Estate’s settings, so the Assistant can say where it is and who answers.

gaps.where: Members → ⋯ beside a teammate → View as <name> (and the phone’s More → View as a teammate)
gaps.gap: Starting View as is rightly kept out (coverage.ts:406-407 teammate_view.start/end). But no Assistant words mention it: grep -i 'view as' finds nothing in packages/core/src/assistant or apps/worker/src/assistant beyond the NEVER/NOT_FOR entries. The team onScreen reads as a full list ('⋯ beside a person has Edit hours, Permissions (owners only), and Remove from workspace', settings-map.ts:443), and PHONE_APP's More line (places-map.ts:625) leaves out View as a teammate, which the phone shows to holders of members.view_as (more.tsx:69,173-177). So the Assistant may say there is no such thing.
gaps.fix: Fixed: Members’ words name View as <their name> (owners and admins, for someone below them, until Stop viewing), with a How to. The phone’s More line names View as a teammate, and manage_team says viewing as a teammate is only ever the person’s to start and stop.

gaps.where: Settings → Safety, Check-ins card: Ask them after, Then tell their contacts after, Who’s told when someone has nobody to tell (hint: The safety person. Nobody picked: the business’s owners and admins.)
gaps.gap: The screen's labels are 'Ask them after', 'Then tell their contacts after' and 'Who’s told when someone has nobody to tell' (hint 'The safety person. Nobody picked: the business’s owners and admins.'). settings-map onScreen uses 'Ask after', 'Tell their contacts after' and 'Safety person'. settings-map what/onScreen, update_safety_settings and the safety.settings query description all say the safety person is told when someone 'has no contacts'. The ladder tells them only when there's no teammate contact still in the business and no outside contact who agreed and hasn't said STOP. So someone whose only contact hasn't replied OK gets the wrong answer.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the settings map, update_safety_settings and the safety.settings words use the screen’s labels (Ask them after, Then tell their contacts after, Who’s told when someone has nobody to tell) and say what nobody to tell means: no teammate contact still in the business, and nobody outside who replied OK and not STOP.

gaps.where: The web’s own My safety page (/safety: Checked in, I’m OK, check me out, +15 min, Who’s told, When), and the phone’s Settings → My safety row
gaps.gap: Real: the web's own My safety page (/app/w/<ws>/safety, title 'My safety': Checked in · place, I’m OK, check me out, +15 min, Who’s told if you don’t check out, When) is named nowhere in the Assistant's words. PHONE_APP's 'Its Settings' line (places-map.ts:625) leaves out the phone's My safety row (settings/index.tsx:260). Overstated: the prompt sentence says the phone's Settings 'holds only the person’s own things (notifications, appearance, their cell)', and My safety is the person's own, so it doesn't contradict the settings-map howTo (settings-map.ts:1021), which already gives the phone way.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the places map has My safety (/safety: Checked in, I’m OK, check me out, +15 min, Who’s told, When), the phone’s Settings line names My safety, and the safety How to says how to see or end your own check-in.

gaps.where: Settings → Permissions: a card for each permission group, including Documents (Send documents to sign, Make document templates)
gaps.gap: The Permissions page draws a card for each PERMISSION_GROUPS title: Contacts, Inbox and calls, Calendar, Money, Documents, Automations and AI, Business and team. The settings-map line leaves out Documents (Send documents to sign, Make document templates).
gaps.fix: Fixed: the Permissions line in the settings map is built from PERMISSION_GROUPS, so every card is named, Documents included, and get_settings permissions lists each card with its permissions’ labels and descriptions.

gaps.where: Invite a teammate → Role: Owner “Full control, including deleting the workspace and managing other Owners.”, Admin “Manages people and settings. Cannot change or remove Owners.”, Member “Works in the workspace. Cannot invite or manage people.”
gaps.gap: ROLE_WORDS on the manage_team card ('Owner — can do everything, including billing', 'Admin — can change how the business is set up', 'Member — works customers, leads and the inbox') and the tool description differ from ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS, which the invite dialog and invite page show. They also suggest admins can't handle billing, but admins hold money.manage, which wallet.top_up needs.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the manage_team card and description use each role’s words from Invite teammate (ROLE_LABELS and ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS).

gaps.where: My safety (web) → When: Tell them again every 10 minutes, for an hour; Settings → Safety: “Then they’re told again every 10 minutes, for an hour”
gaps.gap: get_settings area safety returns only safety.settings (askAfterMinutes, alertAfterMinutes, safetyUserId, safetyPersonName). Neither it nor the settings-map text says that contacts are told again every SAFETY_DEFAULTS.repeatMinutes (10) minutes for an hour, which Settings → Safety and My safety → When both show.
gaps.fix: Fixed: get_settings safety adds repeatMinutes (10) and says contacts are told again every 10 minutes, for an hour, until someone says they’re OK; the settings map says so too.

gaps.where: Safety alert → Where their phone was: On the map, <time> (a https://maps.google.com/?q=lat,lng link)
gaps.gap: It's true that read_safety_alert returns latitude, longitude and locatedAt with no ready-made map link, while the screen shows 'On the map, <time>' linking to https://maps.google.com/?q=lat,lng. But the prompt never forbids building a link: its rule is about names, numbers, dates, amounts and ids (prompt.ts:13). The coordinates and time are all there, so the only thing missing is a ready link.
gaps.fix: Fixed: read_safety_alert’s answer has mapUrl, made by safetyMapLink in @hfos/core, which the ladder’s messages and the alert page’s Where their phone was now use too.

gaps.where: Settings → Permissions (owners only; the page is not found for anyone else)
gaps.gap: readArea always adds 'Not this person's to see: … An owner or admin can.' when a query is refused. For area permissions, permission.settings needs permissions.manage, which only owners hold by default (the page is notFound for anyone else, and set_permissions says 'Owners only'). So an admin is told an admin can see it.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the note for a part someone may not see is built from that part’s own permission, so Settings → Permissions says only an owner can, or someone given it.

gaps.where: The invitation email’s button and the invite page’s button: Accept invitation
gaps.gap: The handover step 'They press Accept and pick how they sign in' is wrong twice over. The email's button is 'Accept invitation' (invitation-email.ts:58; 'Check it and finish' for a handover). /invite is a protected route, so someone signed out signs in or makes an account first (proxy.ts:10-13), then presses Accept invitation on the invite page (accept-invite.tsx:55). The screenRef line is wrong: accept-invite.tsx has 81 lines.
gaps.fix: Fixed: the handover says: they open the email from HandsFreeOS and press Accept invitation; if they aren’t signed in, they sign in or make an account with that email address; they press Accept invitation.

gaps.where: Get help → Ask us for help (In a few words, What happened?, Send it); the ticket carries the page they were on
gaps.gap: It's true that contact_support always sends context {page: 'Ask HandsFreeOS'} (tools-extra.ts:1783), while Get help sends the pathname and platform. ToolContext carries no page (runtime.ts:91-98), so the tool can't add it. But the model sees the page record and writes `details` itself, so it can describe the record in the message. Only the structured page field is missing.
gaps.fix: Fixed: contact_support sends the screen they asked from as the ticket’s page (Ask HandsFreeOS on /app/w/<business>/<screen>), as Get help sends its page.

gaps.where: Get help menu, while Getting started isn’t finished: Getting started, Take the tour, Ask us for help
gaps.gap: Part of this is wrong. The Get help menu's Getting started item is already in the Assistant's words ('Bring Getting started back after hiding it: Get help at the foot of the menu, then Getting started', places-map.ts:47). What is real: Take the tour, in the Get help menu while Getting started isn't finished and on the Getting started card, is named nowhere (grep -i 'tour' finds nothing in packages/core/src/assistant or the prompt). EVERY_PAGE (places-map.ts:607) also describes Get help only as the form.
gaps.fix: Fixed: Take the tour is in the words: the Get help menu (Getting started, Take the tour, Ask us for help) and a Home How to for taking the tour again.

gaps.where: Phone check-in banner: Sharing where you are (until check-out)
gaps.gap: safety.mine's open check-in returns id, appointmentId, place, startedAt, plannedEndAt, state and extendedCount, but not app.safety_checkins.follows or located_at. So 'Am I sharing where I am?' can't be answered. The phone banner itself reads the phone's own followed id (useFollowedCheckIn, use-check-in.ts:34), while the database's follows column is what a query can give.
gaps.fix: Fixed: safety.mine’s open check-in has follows and locatedAt, so read_safety_mine says whether the phone shares where it is and when it was last there.
